trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going to (2,7,4) would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,7,2).
I can't rule out to (6,7,2) or to (4,6,1) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,7,2).
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (7,6,4) would force the line onto number 4 before its turn. So the line goes to (7,4,2).
Going to (6,4,1) would force the line onto number 17 before its turn. So the line goes to (7,4,4).
I can't rule out to (7,2,4) or to (7,4,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (7,2,4).
The line must go to (7,2,6): to (7,2,2) is number 18, which comes later; to (6,1,4) is number 20, which comes later.
Going to (6,1,6), the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 4; going to (6,2,7), the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 4. So the line goes to (7,4,6).
Going to (6,4,7) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,6,6).
Cell (7,6,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,7,4).

Going to (2,6,7) would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (4,4,7) would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (6,6,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,4,7).
Going to (6,2,7) would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,4,7).
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
I can't rule out to (1,4,6) or to (2,2,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (1,4,6).
I can't rule out to (1,2,6) or to (1,4,4) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (1,2,6).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (1,4,4), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going to (2,1,4), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1,4). So my guess (to (1,2,6) from number 8) was wrong, so the line must go to (1,4,4).
Going to (1,4,2), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (1,2,4).
Going to (2,1,4), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1,6). So the line goes to (1,2,6).
The line must go to (2,2,7): to (2,1,6) is number 11, which comes later.
Cell (6,2,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,1,6).
Going to (4,1,4) would strand number 11: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (2,1,6).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,1,4).
Going to (4,1,4) would leave number 12 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (2,1,2).
Going to (2,2,1), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (1,2,2).
Going to (2,2,1), the next 10 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,6,1). So the line goes to (1,4,2).
Going to (2,4,1) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,6,2).
Going to (2,6,1) would force the line onto number 15 before its turn. So the line goes to (1,6,4).
Going to (2,7,4) would force the line onto number 15 before its turn. So the line goes to (1,6,6).
Cell (2,6,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,6).
Going to (4,6,1) would force the line onto number 17 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,4,1).
Cell (2,2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,2,1).
Going to (6,2,1) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes to (4,4,1).
Cell (4,6,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,6,1).
Going to (6,1,2) would turn number 18 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes to (7,2,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,1,2).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 56 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 37 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 35/54 cells (65%).
Generation 1: fitness 31/54. The best line covers 31 cells.
Generation 5: fitness 36/54. The best line covers 41 cells, the first 36 of them still look solvable.

Generation 8: fitness 54/54. The best line covers 54 cells.
Generation 8: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 48 futures: 17% survive going to (4,7,2) (best covers 37%); to (2,7,4) 0%.
Tried 48 futures: 42% survive going to (6,7,2) (best covers 57%); to (4,6,1) 0%.

Jackpot! A future after going to (7,6,6) covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 54 cells x 54 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
